teaser.en: When this climber flowers, whole bushes seem to catch fire, and Digo naming linked it to its tree cousin long before botanists did.

summary.en: *Mkongolo wa kundu* is a scrambling climber with blazing red flower clusters and four-winged pink fruits. Its Digo name ties it to the tree *mkongolo*, a link that botany confirms, since both are *Combretum*.

about.en:
*Mkongolo wa kundu* is a woody scrambler that climbs over shrubs and into small trees. In flower it is unmistakable: dense clusters of brilliant scarlet flowers with long red stamens cover the branches, often when the plant has few leaves, so the colour stands out across the bush. The flowers are rich in nectar and attract sunbirds.

The fruits that follow are papery and four-winged, flushed pink, like those of other *Combretum*. The leaves are broad, simple and opposite.

where.en: Look along forest edges and in riverine thicket, where it climbs over the surrounding vegetation. It is easiest to find in flower, when the red clusters can be seen from far off.

uses.en: No specific Digo use has been recorded.

culture.en: The name *mkongolo wa kundu* means 'red *mkongolo*'. It links the climber to the tree *mkongolo* (*Combretum schumannii*) through their similar flowers. Western botany places both in the same genus, *Combretum*, so this is a neat case where Digo plant naming and scientific classification agree.

names.en: Digo: *mkongolo wa kundu*, 'red *mkongolo*'. English: burning bush. No Swahili name has been recorded. Scientists call it *Combretum paniculatum*.

reason.en: The tree it is named after, also a Combretum
